Hence, you will need to normalise your Firefly luciferase readings to account for the differences in transfection efficiency across your different cell samples.

Glycolysis does not require oxygen, and is therefore an appropriate source of ATP during sprinting. Oxygen is only consumed during oxidative phosphorylation, which is a slow process and therefore not appropriate for sprinting. The rate of oxygen consumption can be used as an indirect measure of energy expenditure, as it is impossible to measure the rate of ATP production directly. The rate of carbon dioxide production can also be used as an indirect measure of energy expenditure, however it is difficult to measure as much of the CO2 produced is exhaled during normal breathing. Creatine phosphate is used to generate ATP anaerobically during the first few seconds of sprinting, and this process involves substrate level phosphorylation.
